title: Your first script
summary: Put commands in a file, make it runnable, and give it arguments.

text: A script is a text file of commands, run from top to bottom.
- The first line, #! (the shebang), says which program reads it.
- chmod +x makes it runnable, ./ runs the one in this folder.
- $1, $2… are the arguments, $# how many there are.

scheme: ││└─ a failure inside a pipe counts
│└── an unset variable is an error
└─── stop at the first failed command
text: By default a script goes on after an error, and the next lines work on a broken state.
- This line makes it stop early and loudly. Put it at the top of your scripts.
- bash -n checks the syntax, bash -x shows each line as it runs.
